title: Isolated worktrees can produce false path-resolution failures when code assumes canonical sibling repo layout
summary: Testing the Human Estimator knowledge-client fix from an isolated worktree (CapitalGlass-BidComposer-worktrees/human-estimator-knowledge-client-fix-v1) produced ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND because the worktree's parent directory differs from the canonical /home/wesley/repos layout the sibling-path arithmetic assumes. This is a testing artifact, not a fix defect -- re-verified correct via an explicit CG_APPBUILDER_MCP_ROOT env override, which produced clean results.
retrievalQuestions: Why does a canonical sibling-repo path resolution fail when tested from an isolated git worktree?
Is an ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND error from an isolated worktree evidence of a real bug in the fix?
How do you correctly test a sibling-path-dependent fix from a worktree whose parent directory differs from the canonical repo layout?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent tests sibling-repo-dependent code from an isolated <repo>-worktrees/<work-package-id> directory and sees a path-resolution failure
startAt: the env-override mechanism the code already exposes (e.g. CG_APPBUILDER_MCP_ROOT)
runPreflight: compare the worktree's parent directory against the canonical /home/wesley/repos layout
doNot: Conclude a sibling-path-dependent fix is broken based solely on a failure observed from an isolated worktree whose parent directory differs from the canonical repo layout
Modify the fix's resolution logic to special-case worktree layouts instead of using the env-override it already supports
proveBeforeClaiming: The same fix, re-tested with the documented env-override (e.g. CG_APPBUILDER_MCP_ROOT) pointed at the real canonical sibling repo, produces a clean successful result
